review.notes: Automated line-level diff of extracted text from all 51 physical PDF pages against the OCR Markdown (case/punctuation/LaTeX-equivalent math normalized), with targeted verification of every flagged page. Bottom-of-page crops of physical pages 2, 13, 16 and 21 were rendered and visually inspected to confirm the footnote bodies; the section 2.5 page-boundary split was verified on rendered physical p.15. No code fences exist in this document and all headings match printed section headings. All 14 printed footnote markers except marker 1 (swallowed next to an emoji glyph on physical p.2) survive in the OCR while every footnote body was dropped; the patches restore all 14 bodies, grouped where their markers sit inside a paragraph that ends in a colon introducing a list (markers 3-6 before the numbered evaluation list, marker 7 inside list item 1). The PDF's own typos ('comparsions', 'competitve', duplicated 'is is' on p.16) were silently corrected by the OCR and left as printed. Remaining diff hits are figure-internal labels (Figures 1, 5, 11, 12 and the architecture/training diagrams) and Unicode-math-versus-LaTeX normalization artifacts, all verified present in the OCR prose.

patches.evidence: Rendered physical p.14 ends mid-sentence '...the savings could reach ∼4T tokens of compute (e.g., ∼2 avoided' and rendered physical p.15 (viewed at 130 dpi) opens with the plain continuation 'runs at 1.5T and ∼2 at 0.5T), or roughly 16% of the total pretraining FLOP budget.' as body text. The OCR promoted the p.15 first line to a '##' heading, splitting the sentence and injecting a spurious section into the table of contents flow; the patch demotes it back into the preceding paragraph.
